title: Hiding a window on close strands foreground + accessibility focus on the invisible window (Windows MSAA/UIA) - screen readers keep reading the closed app
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.4.0; Reproduced in shipping apps on current Electron/Chromium builds (OpenAI Codex, Anthropic Claude desktop).  Codex: Version 26.616.81150 Claude 1.15200.0 (250bae) 2026-06-23T05:40:53.000Z

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (build 26100.8655)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a top-level `BrowserWindow` is hidden in response to a close (e.g. the app intercepts `close` and calls `win.hide()` to keep running in the background), the window should relinquish foreground activation and clear its focused accessibility state. Windows then activates the next window in the Z-order, and that window's process emits `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND`, so assistive technology (Narrator, JAWS, NVDA) follows focus to the new foreground.

### Actual Behavior

On Alt+F4, the window's pixels disappear but it is **hidden, not destroyed**, and it **never relinquishes foreground activation or its focused accessibility state**:

- The top-level window fires `EVENT_OBJECT_HIDE` while still reporting `STATE_SYSTEM_FOCUSED` (state `0x168004`).
- The render-widget child is reparented offscreen (`0x118000`) and moved to the origin.
- No `EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROY` is fired.
- No `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND` to any successor window is fired.
- `GetForegroundWindow()` immediately after the close still returns the now-invisible window's HWND (also visible inline in the events' `ForegroundWnd` field).

Because foreground is never released, Windows never activates a successor, so no process emits a foreground/focus event. Screen readers have nothing to follow and keep reading the closed app. With Narrator, "Say current line" (Insert+Up) still reads the closed window's chat content after the window is gone.


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/v-tab-vispero/640ea5acbf40c6c14ce547b8254d0ee2

### Additional Information

### Sample events

**App A - OpenAI Codex (`codex.exe`)** - trigger then teardown:
```
GetMsgProc hwnd=5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1] WM_SYSCOMMAND (0x0112) wParam=0xF060 {cmd=SC_CLOSE}

MSAAEvent [Object_Hide] Hwnd: 4088e[Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND] OBJID_WINDOW/CHILDID_SELF Role:[Window] State:[Invisible Focusable, 0x108000] ForegroundWnd: 5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel)
MSAAEvent [Object_ParentChange] Hwnd: 4088e[Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND] State:[Invisible OffScreen Focusable, 0x118000] ForegroundWnd: 5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel)
MSAAEvent [Object_LocationChange] Hwnd: 4088e[Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND] Rect:[0,0,1194,820] State:[Invisible OffScreen Focusable, 0x118000] ForegroundWnd: 5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel)
MSAAEvent [Object_Hide] Hwnd: 5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel) OBJID_WINDOW/CHILDID_SELF Name:[Codex] Role:[Window] State:[Focused Invisible Sizeable Moveable Focusable, 0x168004]
MSAAEvent [Object_Hide] Hwnd: 5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel) OBJID_CARET Name:[Edit] Role:[Caret] State:[Invisible, 0x8000]
MSAAEvent [Object_LocationChange] Hwnd: 5089a[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel) State:[Focused Invisible ..., 0x168004]   (x7, window still invisible + FOCUSED)
```

**App B - Anthropic Claude (`claude.exe`)** - identical fingerprint, different event ordering:
```
MSAAEvent [Object_Hide] Hwnd: c0618[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel) OBJID_WINDOW/CHILDID_SELF Name:[Claude] Role:[Window] State:[Focused Invisible Sizeable Moveable Focusable, 0x168004]
MSAAEvent [Object_Hide] Hwnd: c0618[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](topLevel) OBJID_CARET Name:[Edit] Role:[Caret] State:[Invisible, 0x8000]
MSAAEvent [Object_ParentChange] Hwnd: 1004c2[Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND] State:[Invisible OffScreen Focusable, 0x118000] ForegroundWnd: c0618[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](invisible)(topLevel)
MSAAEvent [Object_LocationChange] Hwnd: 1004c2[Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND] Rect:[0,0,1200,800] State:[Invisible OffScreen Focusable, 0x118000] ForegroundWnd: c0618[Chrome_WidgetWin_1](invisible)(topLevel)
```

### Why this points at Electron/Chromium, not the apps
Two unrelated apps from different vendors emit a **bit-for-bit identical** close fingerprint: top-level hidden at `0x168004` (FOCUSED retained while invisible), `OBJID_CARET` hidden at `0x8000`, render widget reparented offscreen at `0x118000` and moved to the origin, no destroy, no foreground handoff, and `ForegroundWnd` left on the invisible top-level. The only differences are event ordering and chatter. Independent app teams do not converge on the same state bitmasks and teardown sequence by coincidence - the behavior originates in the shared Electron/Chromium window-hide path.

### Accessibility impact
Screen-reader users cannot perceive that the window closed, focus is stranded on a dead window, and they continue to hear the closed app with no path back to the real foreground. This affects any Electron app that hides-on-close (Signal/Element/Discord are cited in #48268 on Linux; Codex/Claude/Whisper Flow on Windows).

### Suggested fix
When a `BrowserWindow` is hidden while it is the active/foreground window, the hide path should release foreground activation, clear `STATE_SYSTEM_FOCUSED`, and emit the platform deactivation/focus-out accessibility event so the OS and AT can hand off. 

### Related
- #48268 - Hidden windows present themselves as active to Linux screenreaders (at-spi). Same defect, Linux side.
- #10023 - `win.hide()` does not focus the background window on Windows. `win.blur()` workaround.
- #405 - Restore focus to the previous application, when Cerebro closes
